title: Mini Crackme — 2026-09-08 (Windows x86-64)
blurb:
Challenge: cl holds a single input byte (Windows x64 calling convention, first arg in cl). Find the value of cl that makes check return 1.

check:
    movzx   eax, cl         ; zero-extend the input byte
    cmp     eax, 0x41       ; below 'A'?
    jl      fail
    cmp     eax, 0x5A       ; above 'Z'?
    jg      fail
    sub     eax, 0x14       ; shift the value down by 20
    cmp     eax, 0x3D       ; compare to target
    jne     fail
    mov     eax, 1
    ret
fail:
    xor     eax, eax
    ret

Answer: cl = 'Q' (0x51) -- The two cmp/jl/jg pairs bound cl to the uppercase-letter range 0x41-0x5A before anything else runs; any byte outside 'A'-'Z' takes the fail branch immediately. Working backward from the final check: eax - 0x14 == 0x3D means eax must be 0x3D + 0x14 = 0x51 right before the sub. 0x51 is 'Q', and it already sits inside the 0x41-0x5A range checked earlier, so both bounds checks fall through, the subtraction and comparison match, and check returns 1.
